name: Milk (Other mammals) (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Milk (Other mammals) [Milk and milk products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA SR Legacy 'Goat's milk, whole' NDB 01106 (via nutritionvalue.org 11116000 and foodfact.info amino-acid table)
MilkFacts.info Nutrient Content of Milk Varieties (cow/goat/sheep comparison)
Supplee & Bellis, 'Citric acid content of milk and milk products', J Biol Chem (milk citrate ~0.172%)
Garnsworthy et al., 'Variation of Milk Citrate with Stage of Lactation', J Dairy Sci S0022-0302(06)72227-5
Agrarforschung Schweiz 2008, orotic acid in cow/ewe/goat milk
FooDB FOOD00690 (Milk, other mammals) source record
provenance.curation_notes: Curated as whole goat milk, the representative non-bovine mammalian milk. DOMINANT carbon source is LACTOSE (~4.5 g/100g, ~131 mM); the principal organic acid is CITRATE (~0.15 g/100g, ~7.8 mM, was missing and is a key Ca/Mg buffer + carbon source), with trace orotic/lactic/acetic acids. Casein-rich protein (3.56 g) supplies a full amino-acid pool (Glu/Pro/Leu highest). Distinctive goat-milk signature is abundant medium-chain fatty acids (C6:0-C10:0). Removed plant furanocoumarin, a preservative
curation_added: citric acid (dominant organic acid in milk, ~0.15 g/100g; was absent)
lactic acid + acetic acid (trace in fresh milk, flagged)
lactose quantified (4.5 g/100g, the dominant carbon source)
chloride, choline, niacin, pantothenic acid, folate, vitamin E, vitamin K, biotin amounts

curation_removed.name: Nickel
curation_removed.reason: non-nutritive ultratrace contaminant, not a defined milk growth nutrient

curation_removed.name: Co2+
curation_removed.reason: free cobalt ion is not a milk nutrient pool; cobalt is supplied nutritionally as vitamin B12 (already listed)

curation_removed.name: (R)-Oxypeucedanin
curation_removed.reason: a furanocoumarin from Apiaceae plants; biologically implausible in mammalian milk; FooDB predicted/contaminant

curation_removed.name: epsilon-Polylysine
curation_removed.reason: a microbial-fermentation food preservative additive, not a natural constituent of milk

curation_removed.name: (E)-2-Phenyl-2-butenal
curation_removed.reason: trace Maillard/flavor volatile aldehyde, not a growth nutrient

curation_removed.name: (±)-erythro-Isoleucine
curation_removed.reason: non-physiological stereoisomer/DB artifact; the real nutrient is L-isoleucine (already listed)

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
